name: process-scroll
purpose: The stages of a process as a row of numbered dark cards on a pixel texture, under a section title. On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways with snap; from the large breakpoint up the cards share the width. From the design sample's site `ProcessScroll`.
useWhen: How something works in three to five ordered stages (build, deploy, observe).
avoidWhen: For more than five stages or stages with art — use `FeatureScroll`.
For a row that pins while the page scrolls — use `StickyCarousel`.
related: StickyCarousel` — the same cards, pinned while the row travels.
bestPractices: Name each stage with a verb.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it.

props.name: titleKind
props.doc: Alignment of the section title over the card row.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: descriptionWidth
props.doc: Column span of the paragraph: `wide` runs it across the middle column too.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The stages, in order; each is `{ title, description }` and gets its own numbered card.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the scrollable card row; defaults to the title.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'

  const steps = [
    { title: 'Push', description: 'Every push to the main branch builds a new version.' },
    { title: 'Build', description: 'The build runs in an isolated worker with your settings.' },
    {
      title: 'Deploy',
      description: 'The version goes live everywhere at once, with no regions to pick.'
    },
    { title: 'Observe', description: 'Metrics and logs for the new version arrive in seconds.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ProcessScroll
    eyebrow="How it works"
    title="From commit to production"
    description="Four stages, all automatic once the repository is connected."
    :steps="steps"
  />
</template>
